Authentication settings

Choose which directories (Active Directory, LDAP, FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS) may sign users in and in what order, what profile new directory users get, whether they need approval, and import directory users before their first sign-in.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Access & Identity → Authentication (URL /settings/#tab-auth)

What is it?#

The Authentication tab decides who can prove their identity to SATOM. Besides the local user database (always on), you can enable Active Directory, generic LDAP and FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS as sign-in sources, give them an order, set what happens to a directory user the first time they sign in, and import directory users in advance.

What does it do?#

  • Sign-in sources — the local database (always on, not configurable) plus any of Active Directory, LDAP (generic) and FortiAuthenticator / RADIUS, each with an Order. Sign-in walks the enabled sources in order; the first that accepts the password wins.
  • Default profile and approval gate for directory users created at first sign-in.
  • Connection settings for the LDAP server (shared by AD and LDAP) and for RADIUS.
  • Import scopes — groups/OUs to import, each with the profile its members receive.
  • Test connection — tests one source with the values currently in the form.
  • Sync directory users — imports directory accounts as local rows, created disabled.

❗Important — Local accounts never fall through

A user whose account is local is checked only against the local password and is never sent to a directory. This keeps the built-in administrator usable when every directory is down.

Requirements#

  • users.manage.
  • For AD/LDAP: a reachable LDAP server; for LDAP (generic) a service account (Bind DN) that can search users.
  • For FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS: a RADIUS client entry for SATOM on the FortiAuthenticator, and — for importing users — the FortiAuthenticator registered under Appliances (its API key is reused to read the roster; see FortiAuthenticator).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Saving, testing and syncing (POST /settings/auth, /settings/auth/test, /settings/auth/sync) require users.manage. Users without it do not see the Access & Identity group; direct requests return 403.

How to use#

Enable a directory#

  1. Open Settings → Access & Identity → Authentication.
  2. Under Sign-in sources, tick Active Directory, LDAP (generic) and/or FortiAuthenticator / RADIUS and set each one's Order (1–9). The connection blocks for the ticked sources appear below.
  3. Fill the connection fields (see Configuration).
  4. Set Default profile for new directory users and decide on Require administrator approval for new directory users.
  5. Click Save authentication settings — "Authentication settings saved."

💡Tip — Order matters

An unreachable source burns its whole timeout before the next one is tried, and every source ahead of the winner counts a wrong password against its own lockout policy. Put the source most users use first.

Test a source before saving#

  1. In Test connection, pick the Source to test (one at a time).
  2. Optionally type a test username and test password to verify a full bind.
  3. Click Test connection. The result shows in green or red. Values are taken from the form, unsaved; a blank secret field falls back to the stored secret.

Import directory users#

  1. Add rows under Sync groups / OU DNs (AD/LDAP) or the FortiAuthenticator group table (RADIUS), each with an optional Profile on import (blank = the default profile). No rows means every user the directory exposes.
  2. Save the settings first.
  3. Click Sync directory users. On success you are taken to Users with a flash such as "12 new user(s) imported as disabled (pending approval); 3 already existed."
  4. Enable each imported user (and adjust the profile) under Users.

Configuration#

General#

Field Description Required Example
Sign-in sources → Enabled Tick the external sources to use. None ticked = local only. No AD
Order Position in the sign-in chain, 1–9. A missing or invalid value keeps the source's submitted position. No 1
Default profile for new directory users Profile name given to a directory user created at first sign-in (and to imported users whose group row has no profile). Default readonly; a blank value saves readonly. An unknown name falls back to the default, then readonly — never to a more privileged profile. The placeholder shows readonly. No readonly
Require administrator approval for new directory users ON: a first-time directory sign-in creates the account disabled and refuses entry until an admin enables it. OFF (default): the account is created active. No on

LDAP / Active Directory connection (shown when AD or LDAP is ticked)#

Field Description Required Example
Host LDAP server. Yes dc.example.com
Port Default 389; when blank, 636 if LDAPS is ticked, otherwise 389. No 636
AD domain (Active Directory) Domain used to build the UPN for the AD simple bind. AD example.com
User attribute Login attribute. Blank = sAMAccountName for AD, uid for LDAP. No sAMAccountName
Base DN Search base. LDAP dc=example,dc=com
Bind DN (LDAP service acct) Service account for the search-then-bind style. LDAP cn=svc,dc=example,dc=com
Bind password Stored encrypted; blank keeps the stored value (placeholder ******** (stored - blank keeps)). When a vault is in use, a new value is written to the vault as well, where sign-in reads it. LDAP —
User filter (LDAP, optional) Search filter; {username} is substituted. No (uid={username})
Sync groups / OU DNs Import scopes, each with Profile on import. Duplicates (case-insensitive) are dropped. No cn=waf-admins,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com
LDAPS (SSL) / StartTLS / Verify certificate Transport security. Defaults: off / off / on. No LDAPS on

FortiAuthenticator / RADIUS (shown when RADIUS is ticked)#

Field Description Required Example
RADIUS host FortiAuthenticator (or RADIUS server) address. Yes fac.example.com
Port Default 1812. No 1812
Shared secret Stored encrypted (and in the vault when one is active); blank keeps the stored value. Yes —
NAS identifier Sent in each Access-Request. Blank saves satom. No satom
Roster source (registered FortiAuthenticator) Appliance whose REST API lists users for import. Auto — the only registered FortiAuthenticator (default) works only when exactly one is registered. For import fac-01
Groups to import One row per FortiAuthenticator group with Profile on import. A group the appliance does not have fails the whole import. A user listed by two groups keeps the first row's profile. No waf_users

Example#

🧪Example — AD for operators, local admin as fallback

  1. Tick Active Directory, Order 1. Host dc.example.com, Port 636, LDAPS on, AD domain example.com.
  2. Default profile readonly, approval on.
  3. Sync groups: cn=waf-ops,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com → operator; cn=waf-audit,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com → blank.
  4. Test with a real account, save, then Sync directory users and enable the imported rows on the Users page. The built-in local admin keeps working even if the domain controller is down.

Result#

  • Settings are stored in app_settings under auth.*; audit entries settings.auth, settings.auth_test and settings.auth_sync.
  • At sign-in, a new directory user is created with auth_source set to the accepting source, the default profile and an unusable local password. Existing accounts are never downgraded.
  • Imported users are created disabled (pending approval); existing users are left untouched.
  • A pending user who signs in sees "Your account was imported from the directory but is still awaiting administrator approval."

Troubleshooting#

"Invalid username or password." for a directory user#

Possible causes - The account exists in SATOM as a local account with the same username — local accounts are never checked against a directory. The failure is recorded in the audit log as login.fail. - Every enabled source rejected the bind (each source's reason is recorded in the audit entry login.external_fail).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: every failed local sign-in writes a login.fail audit entry (directory failures keep login.external_fail); a new LDAP bind password is stored in the vault too when one is in use, so sign-in no longer keeps using the old vault copy; and saving this form no longer resets tuned LDAP and RADIUS timeouts to 8 seconds.

Solution 1. Check the user's source on Users. 2. Use Test connection with that user's credentials for each source.

Verification — the test reports success for the source the user belongs to.

"Directory sync needs at least one external authentication source (AD, LDAP or FortiAuthenticator)."#

Solution — tick and save at least one external source before syncing.

"No FortiAuthenticator registered. Add the FAC under Appliances (its API key is reused for the roster)."#

Solution — register the FortiAuthenticator under Appliances, or pick it in Roster source. With two or more registered and Auto selected the sync refuses with "N FortiAuthenticators registered (…) - pick one in Settings -> Authentication."

Import fails naming a group#

Possible causes — a group row names a group the appliance does not have. The whole import is refused and the reply lists the problem group.

Solution — correct or remove the row, save, sync again.

Imported users are refused at sign-in, or users who sign in never appear in an import#

Possible causes — two different places hold a group name, and they do different jobs: - On a FortiAuthenticator / RADIUS source, who may authenticate at all is decided on the authenticator itself (its own authentication policy and group filter). SATOM checks no group at RADIUS sign-in. - Who gets imported is decided by the Groups to import rows (or Sync groups / OU DNs) on this tab.

Change one without the other and the two disagree with no error: users appear in the import and are still refused at the door, or authenticate fine and never appear in an import.

Solution — when you change the group on one side, change it on the other side too.

Verification — Test connection with an imported user's credentials succeeds, and the user appears after Sync directory users.

An imported user has fewer rights than their group row gives#

Possible causes — the user signed in before being imported. A directory user created at first sign-in gets the Default profile for new directory users, because a RADIUS Access-Accept carries no group, and a later import never rewrites an account that already exists.

Solution — set the profile on Users. To avoid it, import users before they first sign in.

Sign-in is slow for everyone#

Possible causes — the first source in the order is unreachable; each attempt waits for its full timeout (8 seconds by default) before trying the next.

Solution — fix the source or move it down the order.

Advanced#

Advanced Storage and behaviour details
  • auth.backends holds the ordered list of external sources; an unreadable value fails closed (local sign-in only).
  • AD and LDAP share one server connection: AD uses a UPN simple bind, LDAP a service-account search plus user re-bind. Ticking both tries both styles against the same server.
  • Connection timeouts (auth.ldap.timeout, auth.radius.timeout, default 8 s, clamped 2–60) have no field on the form; a save keeps the stored timeout, which changes only when a request posts ldap_timeout / radius_timeout.
  • Per-group profiles apply to the importer only: a user who signs in without having been imported gets the default profile, because a RADIUS Access-Accept carries no group.
  • Disabling a source keeps its stored configuration, so re-enabling it restores the settings.
  • Account lockout after repeated failures and two-factor authentication for local accounts are described in Profile: Security and Change Password.
